as_told.title: Stubblebine's PK search and the 'Did you kill my computers' recruitment

plain: Lyn Buchanan, a former US Army sergeant, says that in the 1980s General Albert Stubblebine, an Army general looking for people with the power to move things with the mind, brought him into a remote viewing unit at Fort Meade, Maryland, an Army program that trained people to describe distant places using only the mind. Buchanan says that after computers broke down around him, the general got up in his face and asked, "Did you kill my computers with your mind?" He links the story to The Men Who Stare at Goats, a book and film about the US military's psychic programs.
